Deep Shadow Maps is a shadow mapping technique for volume rendering that stores a curve of volume density (or accumulated alpha) as a function of distance in each pixel, rather than just the depth to the nearest opaque object [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim states that Deep Shadow Maps store a curve of volume density (or accumulated alpha) as a function of distance, rather than just the depth to the nearest opaque object. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'rather than storing the depth from the light to the nearest object... deep shadow maps store the density of the volume instead as a function of distance. In other words, each pixel in the deep shadow maps stores a curve that represents how transmission through the volume changes as we move through it.' Source [S2] corroborates this by explaining that deep shadow maps store an approximation of the shadow function (accumulated alpha/absorption) in a stack of textures, contrasting with standard shadow maps that store depth to the nearest object. Both sources confirm the core mechanism described in the claim.
